To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the morphology, dynamics and potential hotspots of Land Surface Temperatures at a local scale in urban areas can be characterized by using a non-parametric Multi-Scale Shape Analysis.

(1) the temperature patterns are decomposed into fundamental deformation modes, which allows for a process-based understanding; and (2), the local land surface temperatures are identified by using a triplet of shape, curvature, and temperature.

(1) The Multi-Scale Gaussian Process Modeling can effectively decompose the latent Land Surface Temperature patterns into fundamental modes; (2) The local heat islands can be identified morpho-dynamically; (3) The local morphological deformations are correlated with the land surface composition; and (4) The morphological deformations can be associated with the yearly behavior of the local land surface temperatures.

the characterization of the UHI in terms of morphology and dynamics.
the characterization of the urban heat islands at local scales.
